<jats:p>
                    We present a detailed kinematic study of a sample of 32 massive (9.5 ⩽ log(
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>*</jats:sub>
                    /M
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    ) ⩽ 10.9) main sequence star-forming galaxies (MS SFGs) at 4 <
                    <jats:italic>z</jats:italic>
                    < 6 from the ALMA-CRISTAL programme. The data consist of deep (up to 15 hr observing time per target), high-resolution (∼1 kpc) ALMA observations of [C 
                    <jats:sc>II</jats:sc>
                    ]158 μm line emission. This dataset allowed us to carry out the first systematic, kiloparsec-scale (kpc-scale) characterisation of the kinematics nature of typical massive SFGs at these epochs. We find that ∼50% of the sample are disk-like, with a number of galaxies located in systems of multiple components. Kinematic modelling reveals these main sequence disks exhibit high-velocity dispersions (
                    <jats:italic>σ</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>0</jats:sub>
                    ), with a median disk velocity dispersion of ∼70 km s
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>V</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>rot</jats:sub>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>σ</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>0</jats:sub>
                    ∼ 2, which is consistent with dominant gravity driving. The elevated disk dispersions are in line with the predicted evolution based on Toomre theory and the extrapolated trends from
                    <jats:italic>z</jats:italic>
                     ∼ 0–2.5 MS star-forming disks. The inferred dark matter (DM) mass fraction within the effective radius
                    <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>DM</jats:sub>
                    (<
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>e</jats:sub>
                    ) for the disk systems decreases with the central baryonic mass surface density. This is consistent with the trend reported by kinematic studies at
                    <jats:italic>z</jats:italic>
                     ≲ 3; roughly half the disks display
                    <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>DM</jats:sub>
                    (<
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>e</jats:sub>
                    )≲ 30%. The CRISTAL sample of massive MS SFGs provides a reference of the kinematics of a representative population and extends the view onto typical galaxies beyond previous kpc-scale studies at
                    <jats:italic>z</jats:italic>
                     ≲ 3.
                  </jats:p>
